title: OpenAI ChatBridge: deterministic request normalization and response harmonization for Chat Completions compatibility
creator: Maya Patel
description: Implement a compatibility gateway (ChatBridge) that translates between Redwood's core API shape and the OpenAI Chat Completions request/response model. The gateway must: normalize incoming OpenAI-style requests into Redwood internal call shapes, support streaming token deltas mapped to incremental chat messages, preserve and surface function/tool calling semantics (including function name + JSON args), produce structured output (JSON schema enforcement) when requested, and map OpenAI error codes/statuses to Redwood error responses. The implementation should be resilient to partial/ambiguous inputs from clients that expect OpenAI semantics and should fail closed for security-sensitive fields.
acceptance_criteria: Requests with messages array (role/name/content) are correctly normalized to Redwood message model with deterministic role mapping (user/system/assistant/tool)
Streaming chunks produced by Redwood runtime are transformed into delta events matching OpenAI chunk structure: content deltas, role changes, and function_call chunks when applicable

Function calling: when client provides functions + function_call=auto/none/explicit, ChatBridge triggers the right internal tool invocation or surfaces a function call response identical in shape to OpenAI's spec
Structured outputs: prompt-level schema requests (e.g., "response_schema") result in post-generation validation and explicit schema diagnostics in responses
Edge-case behaviors (n>1, stop tokens, max_tokens, logprobs, temperature) produce consistent, documented semantics and unit tests
Comprehensive integration tests against a lightweight OpenAI-compat test harness are included and stable in CI
tasks: Spec: finalize ChatBridge request/response translation matrix (confluence link in links)
Implementation: stateless gateway service that sits in front of the runtime and SDK handlers
Runtime adaptors: streaming delta mapper and function_call serializer/deserializer
Tests: unit tests for single-request mapping, streaming tests with simulated interruptions, function call roundtrip tests
Docs: update SDK docs with OpenAI compatibility notes and caveats
Rollout: staged canary with telemetry flags and traffic split (10% -> 50% -> 100%)
comments: 2025-02-21 Maya Patel: Initial spec draft posted. Key open questions: should the gateway mutate user-supplied function args to conform to schema or return validation errors? Recommendation: return structured validation errors with an option to auto-coerce in a future opt-in flag.

2025-02-22 Luca Moreno: Implementation proposal: lightweight HTTP gateway implemented in Go, reusing existing tokenizers and runtime client. Streaming implemented via server-sent events (SSE) internally, translated to chunked TCP stream to match SDK expectations. Concern: added latency from extra hop — mitigations include keeping gateway in same VPC and pinning to runtime node for session affinity.

2025-02-23 Ana Rodriguez (PM): Product decision: preserve OpenAI field names in top-level responses (e.g., id, model, choices[]) to minimize SDK churn. Add explicit disclaimer in docs for differences in behavior around n and stop sequences under batching.
2025-02-24 Design review: DES-411 suggested a small change to function_call error reporting to include path to failing key. Accepting change, will add to acceptance criteria and tests.

2025-02-25 Security review note: sensitive fields (client_provided_metadata, ephemeral keys) must be stripped before logs. KMS-encrypted function args flagged and not logged in plaintext. Action: add a pre-log scrubber in gateway middleware.
notes: Implementation alternatives considered: (A) in-process SDK shim (low latency, more SDK changes), (B) dedicated gateway service (higher isolation, easier rollout). Chosen: dedicated gateway to centralize compatibility logic and allow independent rollout.

Streaming behavior: Redwood's runtime emits token-level deltas with optional role/finish_reason flags. ChatBridge will batch small deltas (<=3 tokens) into single OpenAI chunk where possible to reduce overhead. If a function_call begins mid-stream, gateway emits a function_call chunk with name and incremental args encoded as partial JSON; finalization occurs when finish_reason indicates function_call_complete.

Function calling harmonization: Redwood tools have metadata (name, schema, allowed_roles). ChatBridge enforces schema validation on tool outputs and returns schema mismatch diagnostics as 'choices[].finish_reason = "tool_schema_mismatch"' with a top-level 'validation' object in the response for troubleshooting.

Errors mapping: map Redwood internal codes to OpenAI-ish codes. Example: internal RATE_LIMIT -> "429" with message and 'type': 'rate_limit'. Auth errors map to 401/403 equivalents. Internal transient errors implement exponential backoff header to guide clients.
Telemetry: add metrics for 'compat:request_type', 'compat:streaming_chunks', 'compat:function_calls', 'compat:schema_validations' to monitor parity regressions and customer impact

Backward compatibility: SDKs that use the older /v1/chat/completions shape should continue working without changes; add a deprecation timeline only if we need to change top-level fields in future major revision
review_feedback: Eng lead (Priya Nair): please add benchmarks for additional latency introduced by gateway under 1k RPS. Target: p95 added latency < 12ms in same region

Infra (Samir Khan): gateway must be containerized with readiness/liveness probes and use IAM roles for runtime access. Also require a circuit-breaker to avoid cascading failures into runtime under partial outage
Docs (Eleni Park): include explicit examples for streaming conversion and function_call sample with nested JSON args
